text:
anya: heads-up — seeing big host CPU spikes in staging when clients stream lots of tiny chunks (2-4 token emits).
kevin: yep, noticed correlation. ingress gRPC decode shows hot loops in frame parsing and header handling.
sumi: is this tokenizer or network framing? could be clients splitting aggressively.
jack: profiled with perf + flamegraph — most time in grpc::Http2Decoder::ProcessData and our protobuf framer. not in zlib.
kevin: sample log snippet:
```
[2026-03-15T09:12:03Z] req=abc stream=12 parse_time_ms=18 frame_count=6
[2026-03-15T09:12:03Z] req=def stream=7 parse_time_ms=4 frame_count=1
[2026-03-15T09:12:03Z] req=ghi stream=4 parse_time_ms=29 frame_count=12
```
perf-bot: nightly perf: host_parse_latency (staging) p50 +12% vs base on commit abc123 — alert created.
anya: also saw KV cache miss rate briefly spike with these small-chunk traffic patterns. suspect we recreate per-chunk keys or evict due to many tiny entries.
jack: confirmed: we serialize same request metadata per chunk: code is basically `for chunk in chunks: write(meta); write(payload)` — repeated allocations and memcpy.
sumi: two quick mitigations: client-side coalescing (increase batch threshold) or server-side coalescing (merge small frames into a single parse unit). server-side is lower friction.
kevin: we have HTTP/1 coalesce at ingress, but not HTTP/2/gRPC. adding a small reassembly buffer for stream frames should be cheap. suggestion: coalesce up to 5ms or 256 bytes.
anya: cheap heuristic: merge consecutive frames <64 bytes arriving within 5ms into one parse op. avoids extra protobuf framing and reduces KV churn.
jack: also flagging runtime interaction: excessive host CPU reduces cores available to batching threadpool, which can push the model runtime to suboptimal kernel selection for small batches. different pain but related.
kevin: yep — if host threads steal cycles, runtime might fallback to single-threaded kernels or small-batch kernels that are less efficient.
sumi: proposed plan: 1) ingress coalescing patch for grpc/http2 (5ms, 256B cap) 2) change tokenizer to append into a lazy buffer (avoid immediate decode per chunk) 3) add metrics: chunk_coalesce_count, avg_coalesced_bytes, per-stream_frame_count 4) run perf job.
anya: opening PR now, will tag reviewers and include microbench harness. @kevin @jack can you review once up?
infra-bot: deploy-bot: started rollout to staging for `coalesce-chunks-5ms` at 1802456845.
jack: quick local smoke — p95 parse went from 42ms -> 9ms with coalescing + lazy buffer :thumbsup:. KV_cache_miss rate also dropped in the run.
perf-bot: perf-run complete: staging host_parse_latency p50 -9%, p95 -32%, KV_cache_miss -7% (compared to previous nightly).
kevin: nice. can we also add a fallback gate so clients that depend on chunk boundaries (rare) still work? maybe preserve explicit chunk boundaries when header `x-preserve-chunks: true` is set.
anya: good call — will add opt-out header. also adding integration test that streams single-token chunks with and without header.
sumi: after merge let's observe 24h and then consider backport to dedicated infra.
anya: will monitor dashboards, added alerts for chunk_coalesce_rate and host_cpu_spike. closing here unless new regressions crop up. :eyes:
